meaning_by_symbol.P1: Sound a sustained {I} tone near all six faces simultaneously for {T} seconds, starting from the {S} face. Let the tone fade naturally and wait for the hum to stabilize.
meaning_by_symbol.P2: Chime a bell near two opposite faces, starting from the {S} face. Alternate the chime between the two faces — {T} seconds pause between chimes — for five cycles at {I} tone.
meaning_by_symbol.P3: Drape a cloth over two adjacent edges near the {S} face for {T} seconds at {I} coverage. Then chime a bell three times near the {S} face.
meaning_by_symbol.P4: Warm each corner of the {S} face by holding a heated stone nearby for {T} seconds at {I} warmth, in sequence. Then trace each edge of the {S} face with a finger.
meaning_by_symbol.P5: Place a warm stone beside the {S} face at {I} warmth for {T} seconds. Rotate and repeat for each face.
meaning_by_symbol.P6: Drape a cool cloth over the Veyru for {T} seconds. Remove the cloth and fan {I} cool air across the {S} face and the opposite face for {T} seconds.
meaning_by_symbol.P7: Illuminate the {S} face with a dim lamp and the opposite face with a bright lamp simultaneously at {I} brightness for {T} seconds, without moving the lamps.
meaning_by_symbol.P8: Drape a folded cloth over the {S} face for {T} seconds at {I} coverage. Then chime a bell near each edge of the {S} face twice.
meaning_by_symbol.P9: At each corner of the {S} face, chime a bell briefly at {I} tone, then warm the two edges meeting at that corner with a heated stone for {T} seconds.
meaning_by_symbol.P10: Rest a flat board against the {S} face at {I} contact for {T} seconds. Rotate and repeat for each face-pair.
meaning_by_symbol.P11: Chime a bell near the center of each face once at {I} tone, starting from the {S} face. Then place a warm stone beside the Veyru for {T} seconds.
meaning_by_symbol.P12: Place the Veyru on a soft surface with the {S} face up at {I} contact. Let it rest undisturbed for {T} seconds.
meaning_by_symbol.P13: Drape a cool cloth over the Veyru for {T} seconds. Remove and fan {I} cool air across all six faces for {T} seconds, starting from the {S} face.
meaning_by_symbol.P14: Rotate the Veyru slowly over {T} seconds while sounding a steady tone at {I} volume near opposite faces, starting from the {S} face. After rotation, chime a bell once near each corner.
meaning_by_symbol.BC/T/CH: bright corner or bright corners, ticking, and corner heat
meaning_by_symbol.OP/2H/EF: opposite-face bright/dark pulse, two-tone hum, and edge flash
meaning_by_symbol.BF/HW/LV: one bright face, high whine, and local vibration
meaning_by_symbol.TB/LH/FF: too bright, layered hum, and frozen faces
meaning_by_symbol.CT/AP/SE: clashing tones, alternating patterns, and shimmering edges
meaning_by_symbol.RF/BH/CS: random face flicker, broken hum, and chaotic surfaces
meaning_by_symbol.D/WH/WO: dim, whisper hum, and washed-out patterns

reply.rationale: No defensible multi-entry compositional paradigm survives the evidence tests. The P1–P14 forms fail the opaque index test: the numerals do not contribute literal count meaning to the whole symbol, but merely pick out different stored procedures. Thus P1, P2, ... P14 are lexical labels, not P + NUMBER. The slash forms (e.g. BC/T/CH, OP/2H/EF) are suggestive, but the supposed slots do not support stable semantic substitution classes across the family: the first position mixes visual and auditory meanings (e.g. BC 'bright corner(s)' vs CT 'clashing tones'), and the second/third positions likewise do not maintain a consistent role. Shared separators alone are not sufficient evidence. Standalone items such as g/m/s/f and face labels are key-like lexical entries, but there are no actual coded multi-morpheme entries in this dataset where they alternate inside a shared frame. Therefore the safest complete analysis is a flat lexicon.
